articles.title: Karnataka Voter ID Scam: R Ashoka of BJP flags Rs 20 crore irregularity, demands CBI probe
articles.description: BENGALURU: Leader of the Opposition R. Ashoka has accused the Congress government of being involved in an alleged Rs 20-crore irregularity in the printing of 90 lakh voter identity cards in Bengaluru, despite the proposed Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. He has demanded a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into the matter, questioning why such a large number of cards were printed when the voter list was due for revision. Addressing a press conference on Wednesday, Ashoka released documents relating to the tender process and alleged irregularities in the printing of voter identity cards by the State Election Commission. He claimed that the expenditure was unnecessary and that the tender had been issued in violation of financial procedures. The allegations have raised questions about the timing of the printing exercise, the basis on which the cards were prepared and their intended beneficiaries. Read More: Karnataka HC quashes government takeover of Gali Anjaneya Swamy Temple in Bengaluru Ashoka alleged that the Congress government had been embroiled in a series of controversies during its three-and-a-half-year tenure, referring to alleged irregularities in the Valmiki Development Corporation and the excise department. He claimed that the latest case involved the State Election Commission and called for a thorough investigation into the use of public funds. According to Ashoka, the State Election Commission initiated the printing of voter identity cards, described as SVIC cards, for voters in Bengaluru. A single tender was reportedly issued for printing 90 lakh cards. He alleged that the process did not follow the prescribed financial procedures and questioned whether the expenditure was justified when the electoral rolls were expected to undergo revision. Ashoka said that the normal procedure should involve visiting households, collecting updated information and photographs, and then printing identity cards based on verified records. However, he alleged that the authorities relied on the electoral rolls prepared for the previous Lok Sabha election instead of undertaking a fresh verification exercise. He pointed to the timing of the tender as a key issue. According to the documents cited by him, the Election Commission of India issued an order on May 14, 2026, concerning the proposed SIR exercise. The very next day, on May 15, the State Election Commission reportedly invited tenders for printing the voter identity cards. A work order was issued on May 29. Ashoka questioned why the tender was initiated immediately after the announcement relating to the electoral roll revision. He also referred to an affidavit reportedly filed by the State Election Commission before the Supreme Court, stating that local body elections would be conducted after the SIR process was completed and the revised electoral rolls became available. He argued that the sequence of events required closer scrutiny. If the authorities were aware that a fresh revision of electoral rolls was imminent, he asked, why was the printing of 90 lakh cards undertaken using an earlier electoral list? He demanded that officials explain the decision-making process, the financial approvals and the justification for awarding the contract. 31 lakh excess cards: Ashoka The Opposition leader’s principal argument centred on the difference between the number of voters reportedly remaining in Bengaluru after the SIR exercise and the number of identity cards printed by the State Election Commission. Ashoka cited a figure of 59,09,775 voters in Bengaluru after the revision, stating that names of people who had shifted residences or changed addresses had been removed from the rolls. Against this figure, he alleged, the State Election Commission had printed 90 lakh voter identity cards. Based on these numbers, Ashoka claimed that there was a difference of nearly 31 lakh cards. He questioned who would receive the additional cards and why they had not been distributed even after the printing exercise had been completed. He alleged that approximately Rs 20 crore had been spent on the exercise and claimed that the expenditure had become wasteful because the cards were printed without adequately accounting for the revised voter population. He demanded an explanation from the government on the number of cards printed, the records used, the distribution plan and the money spent. Ashoka also linked the alleged discrepancy to the Congress party’s political campaign over voter-list irregularities. Referring to Rahul Gandhi’s repeated allegations of ‘vote chori’, he challenged the Congress leader to visit Bengaluru and oversee the distribution of the newly printed cards. “If Bengaluru has around 59 lakh voters, why were 90 lakh cards printed?” was the question Ashoka raised, demanding that the government clarify the whereabouts and intended use of the remaining cards. He alleged that the difference indicated the possibility of bogus voter identity cards and claimed that the government should establish where the additional 31 lakh cards were located. However, the difference between the number of cards printed and the number of voters on a revised roll does not, by itself, establish that bogus cards were issued or that votes were manipulated.

articles.title: Government working to utilise procurement process for promoting startups: DPIIT Secretary
articles.description: Elaborating on the move to enhance participation of startups in government procurement, DPIIT Additional Secretary Ateesh Kumar Singh said that there are already certain facilities available in the form of relaxations to the GFR (General Financial Rules).

articles.title: Government working to utilise procurement process for promoting startups: DPIIT Secretary
articles.description: The Indian government aims to use procurement processes to promote startups within the nation effectively. Over 2.5 lakh startups exist in the country, with many in smaller towns. National Startup Awards 6.0 will award winning startups a cash prize of Rs 25 lakh across various categories. The initiative seeks to enhance support through mentorship, investor connections, and market access.
